newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods flat amid thin trade Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods flat amid thin trade Tuesday.

text.p: U.S. West Coast wholesale product prices were flat Tuesday, as traders waited to see the direction of the NYMEX March crude contract and how refinery maintenance programs were progressing, brokers said.

Meanwhile, product futures gave the market mixed signals traders said, leaving activity thin. NYMEX February gasoline rose 0.21 cents a gallon on technical buying, while heating oil contracts eased about 0.91 cents a gallon to 66.03 cents.
CARB gasoline in Los Angeles was heard done at 78 cents a gallon yesterday, but no deals were stuck Tuesday with offers notionally flat at 79 cents.
Conventional gasoline in L.A. was offered at 75 cents, unchanged.
Traders said gasoline volumes on the market would ease during the second cycle of February, as fewer winter blending components were added, dropping the volume of gasoline production.
Market players also waited to see the results of the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) inventory report, which was pushed back from Tuesday until Wednesday.
